phones.description: Next-Gen 4nm Performance, Cinematic AI Video Generation, and a Blinding 8,000-Nit Visual Experience The HONOR 600 is a Powerhouse premium mid-ranger, carving out its place as one of the most compelling smartphones of 2026. HONOR doesn’t compromise on eye health either; it integrates a risk-free 3840Hz PWM dimming layer to eliminate screen flicker in low light, alongside an AI Defocus display layer designed to reduce eye strain and provide motion sickness relief Capture the true ambiance of the night with the flagship 200MP Ultra-Clear AI Main Camera. Armed with an f/1.9 aperture, hardware OIS, and a 1/1.4-inch sensor, it utilizes advanced AI RAW models to pull jaw-dropping detail out of pitch-black scenes. Backed by AI Super Zoom 2.0, it easily scales up to 30x digital zoom with cloud-assisted texture recovery. Up front, the 50MP Portrait Selfie Camera ensures every facial detail is beautifully preserved. HONOR 600 Key Features Next-Gen Snapdragon 7 Gen 4: Highly efficient 4nm chip optimized for high-tier gaming and lightning-fast AI tasks. AI Image to Video 2.0: Generate stylized short videos or interpolate a scene using up to three starting photo references. 8,000 Nits Peak AMOLED Screen: A jaw-dropping 1.5K display with ultra-narrow 0.98mm borders for ultimate immersion 200MP AI Dual Camera: Flagship-level main sensor with Optical Image Stabilization (OIS) and advanced night portrait enhancements. 7,000mAh Long-Life Battery: Multi-day power packed into an elegantly slim 7.8mm unibody design. IP68 / IP69 / IP69K Protection: Maximum armored security capable of resisting deep submersion and high-pressure steam jets. It is equipped with the Unisoc T7250 octa-core processor made using the 12nm fabrication process. It has a 6.74-inch 90Hz display with a Panda Glass cover over it and the ArmorShell body that possesses MIL-STD-810H certification and can survive a fall from 1.8 meters. PRODUCT DESCRIPTION Huge 6,300mAh Battery & 15W Quick Charge The Realme Note 80 is designed to provide long-lasting performance with the revolutionary 6,300mAh battery that it comes with in a lightweight 7.94mm device. It lets you enjoy up to 20 hours of video playback continuously or a few days of calling and texting without requiring a charge. The device comes with a 15W fast charger inside the retail box, including the 6W reverse fast charging that allows you to recharge small gadgets, such as wireless earphones and fitness bands in cases of emergencies. ArmorShell Rugged Engineering & Military-Grade Reliability Crafted to survive daily mishaps, the Note 80 is designed using Realme’s ArmorShell architecture, which has been certified as able to survive falls from 1.8 meters onto hard surfaces. It features verified military certification for MIL-STD-810H against thermal shocks, vibrations, and impacts, combined with IP54 certification for protection against water, light rain, and dust. 6.74-Inch 90Hz Display with Smart Touch Technology & Unisoc T7250 The device comes with a large 6.74-inch HD+ display which supports 90Hz refresh rate and reaches peak brightness of 563 nits. Thanks to Smart Touch technology, the touchscreen remains responsive even when user fingers are wet or sweaty. The smartphone is powered by a Unisoc T7250 octa-core processor (2x Cortex-A75 cores and 6x Cortex-A55 cores) combined with a Mali-G57 GPU providing decent performance for daily apps. Other features include a side-mounted fingerprint scanner, a microSD card slot, and a 3.5mm audio jack. Side Fingerprint Reader: Very fast and convenient physical biometric unlock option placed in the power button. 3.5mm Audio Jack and Separate MicroSD Slot: Good compatibility with sound and possibility to enhance the memory. PRODUCT DESCRIPTION Massive 7,500mAh Battery with 45W Turbo & 22.5W Reverse Power The REDMI 17 5G boasts a remarkable 7,500mAh battery that lasts longer than other batteries on the market, thanks to a high-density cell. The phone is designed for individuals who use their devices for long periods, such as delivery personnel, professional users, and gamers, since users can enjoy 2+ days of normal use (the battery can last up to 109 hours of music playback or 28 hours of video streaming at once). 6.9-Inch Display With a Refresh Rate of 120 Hz, Stereo Audio, and 50 MP Camera The massive display measures 6.9 inches in HD+ resolution and sports the 120Hz Adaptive Sync refresh rate. It can produce brightness of up to 825 nits, and the display is protected by Corning Gorilla Glass 7i. You do not need to worry about finger control issues because Wet Touch will always take care of that even if your hands are damp. Not to mention, this smartphone comes with dual stereo speakers that give you three times the volume of conventional speakers. Your photography gets much better thanks to a 50MP AI dual rear camera (f/1.8) that can take daylight images, portraits, and video. MAJOR SPECIFICATIONS 7,500mAh Super Battery: Provides battery operation of over 2 days on a single charge. 45W Quick Charge & 22.5W Reverse Charge: Quickly charge the device and power it up and other appliances through cables. Snapdragon 4 Gen 5 (4nm) 5G: A powerful octa-core processor that provides smooth operation and less heat. 6.9" 120Hz AdaptiveSync Display: A large screen with Gorilla Glass 7i, eye-care certification, and Wet Touch response. 50MP AI Dual Camera: High-res primary camera and 8MP selfie camera. Dual Stereo Speakers (300% Increase in Sound): Loud and clear sound from the speakers, equipped with a 3.5mm headphone jack. IP64 Water and Dust Resistance: Daily protection against accidental water and dust exposure. phones.description: The 6.9-inch Entertainment King with a Massive 6300mAh Battery and Next-Gen HyperOS 3. The Redmi A7 Pro 4G is the first-ever “Pro” model in Xiaomi’s entry-level A-series, officially launched in early 2026. This device is designed for users who want maximum screen size and battery life at an affordable price point. In Nepal, it stands as a robust alternative to the standard Redmi A7, offering a significantly larger display and enhanced software features like HyperOS 3 Redmi A7 Pro 4G Description The Redmi A7 Pro 4G breaks the mold for budget smartphones in 2026. Featuring a massive 6.9-inch HD+ display, it provides a cinema-like experience in the palm of your hand. Whether you are streaming movies, browsing social media, or attending online classes in Kathmandu, Pokhara, Dharan, etc., the 120Hz refresh rate ensures every scroll and animation is smooth and lag-free For the first time, an A-series device launches with Xiaomi HyperOS 3 (based on Android 16). This brings advanced AI tools like Circle to Search with Google and Google Gemini integration to a budget-friendly device. The new Xiaomi Hyper stand feature also offers a dynamic way to track notifications and multitask, similar to flagship models. Built for the heavy user, the 630mAh mega battery is one of the largest in its segment, capable of providing up to 49 hours of call time or 35 hours of video playback. With 15W fast charging and 7.5W reverse wired charging, it can even act as an emergency power bank for your Redmi Buds or other accessories. Upgrade Today and enjoy the biggest and boldest Redmi A-Series yet Redmi A7 Pro Key Features 6.9” 120Hz Immersive Screen: A huge display with 800 nits peak brightness and TUV Rhineland eye-comfort certification. 6300mAh High-Density Battery: Long-Lasting power that retains over 80% capacity even after 1,000 charging cycles. Unisoc T7250 Octa-Core Chipset: Efficient 12nm performance optimized for smooth daily multitasking and light gaming. HyperOS 3 (Android): Modern, fluid interface with built-in AI productivity tools and Google integration. 13MP AI Dual Camera: Features HDR+, Night Mode, and AI Sky replacement for creative Social media photos. IP52 Dust & Splash Resistance: Durable build quality designed to survive daily spills and dusty environments. phones.description: Overview Find the official mobile price in Nepal with updated MRP listings of all available smartphones. These are official prices set by authorised distributors. You can buy these models from the GBN Store. Mobile Brands in Nepal In Nepal, people can buy phones from every brand. The smartphone market in Nepal wide selection of options. People can buy the phone they like. They can pick a budget phone or a very expensive phone. Nepal's smartphone market has standard budget phones and expensive premium phones. People in Nepal can buy phones from Samsung , Apple , Honor , OnePlus , Xiaomi , Vivo , Realme , Infinix , Poco , Motorola , ZTE , Ai +, Tecno, and Nothing . These phones are sold by our GBN Store with various additional services. These days, smartphones have lots of options. This makes consumers choose between a product that is made for them according to their needs and budgets. Some brands provide excellent value for money, and others focus on giving a premium experience to their users. A normal, functional phone typically focuses on reliable performance, a decent camera, and enough battery and storage to handle everyday tasks without extra frills. Premium features, on the other hand, include refined design, advanced camera systems, high-end gaming performance, long battery life, and larger storage capacities. Likewise, many phones today focus on providing built-in AI features. In today's market, with competition at an extreme level, we see phone brands introducing better hardware, software, and exclusive features at unbelievable prices to stay at the top. Thus, even if you are a student looking for a budget phone, a gamer looking for peak performance, or a photographer looking for a camera with great features, rest assured cause Nepal's smartphone market has a wide variety of phones to offer, and understanding each brand would help make a smarter choice. Here is a list of the market share of smartphones in Nepal as of May 2026: Apple: Apple iPhones were introduced in the Nepali market in December 2014. Generation Next Communication (GenXT) was officially introduced as the distributor in Nepal. iPhones were introduced to Nepal after Samsung, so consumers perceive iPhones as a stronger status-symbol brand than a value brand. Despite its high price, people love it, and it holds the highest market share at 24.98 per cent. Xiaomi: Xiaomi came into the Nepalese market in October 2018, with Ramesh Corp’s Tele becoming the official partner. Later, Teletalk was introduced to become a second distributor to break the price monopoly. Today, Xiaomi has a 19.49 percent market share, making it a go-to brand for budget and mid-range phone buyers. Samsung: Samsung entered Nepal in the year 2001 through IMS Group as an official distributor. Mobile phone usage surged after Ncell, formerly known as Mero Mobile, launched. Samsung, being the early mover,r had an advantage, becoming the “safe choice” brand for Nepal, providing phones in every price segment. Fast forward to today, Samsung has a default recommendation for first-time phone buyers and has a 17.73 percent market share in the market. Realme: Realme had a great start when it was introduced to Nepal’s market in 2019 through Jagadamba Mobiles. It had a bad reputation for overpricing in the beginning. The reputation once lost was regained when realme India partnered with Shaker Group in 2021. Today, realme has a 6.19 percent market share in Nepal. Young people and students really like realme because of its design and specs. Vivo: Vivo entered the Nepali market a bit later than Samsung and Xiaomi and built its identity around camera-focused marketing. It particularly advertised its selfie cameras (V-series). It's perceived as a solid mid-range choice, especially for buyers who prioritise photography over raw specs, though it competes closely with Xiaomi and Realme for the same budget-conscious crowd with 5.58 percent market share. Different types of mobile phones available in Nepal In Nepal, mobile phones come in various types that are suitable for people in accordance with their needs, budget, and lifestyle. Whether you need a simple phone for communication or a high-performance phone for demanding tasks, we have options for you. Feature Phones – They are basic phones for calling, texting, FM radio, and long battery life. These phones are valued for their durability and long-lasting battery backups. They remain a popular choice for elderly people and as a backup phone for others. Popular examples in Nepal include the Nokia 105 and Nokia 3310. Entry-Level Smartphones – These are Affordable Android phones for everyday use, typically priced between NPR 20,000 and 25,000. They can handle basic tasks such as handling calls, messaging, social media, and light browsing without issues. Popular models in this category include Redmi 15C and Realme C-series. Mid-Range Smartphones – These smartphones provide balanced performance, camera, and battery for most users, and they are usually priced between NPR 25,000 - 50,0000. This is currently the most competitive segment in Nepal, with brands packing in AMOLED displays and 5G support. Popular picks in this segment include the Redmi Note 15, Samsung Galaxy A17 5G, and Pova 6. Flagship Smartphones – This category contains premium phones with top-tier performance, camera, and displays, which are priced above NPR 100,000. They run on the latest processors such as the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 and Apple A19 or A19 Pro, with software updates for years. Leading examples of Flagship Smartphones in Nepal include the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, iPhone 17 Pro Max, and OnePlus 15. Gaming Smartphones – They are smartphones packed with powerful processors, high-refresh-rate displays, and advanced cooling for gamers. These phones also include extra built-in features such as shoulder trigger buttons. Esports games such as PUBG, Mobile Legends, and Call of Duty run smoothly on them. In Nepal, gaming-focused buyers usually go for iPhones and Samsung Galaxy S Series, alongside the dedicated gaming brands like Nubia's Red Magic series. Camera-Centric Smartphones – Camera-centric smartphones focus on high-quality photography and videography over other specs. Specifications such as Larger Camers Sensors, telephoto lenses, and 4K resolution video recording make them stand out. The Vivo X300 Pro, with its Zeiss-tuned optics and 200MP periscope lens, is a standout example in Nepal, and iPhones are also widely favoured for their reliable video stabilisation. Foldable Smartphones – They are Phones with folding or flip displays for enhanced portability and multitasking. Such phones offer a wide screen that offers more room for productivity while still staying compact in our pockets. The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold series remains the dominant foldable option available in Nepal. 5G Smartphones – Even though Nepal hasn't yet introduced 5G networks in Nepal, still Smartphones that support fifth-generation mobile networks for faster internet speeds are commonly seen nowadays in Nepal’s market. Owning such a phone may seem advantageous as Nepal's telecom infrastructure continues to expand, and we may see 5G networks soon. Rugged Smartphones – They are phones built to withstand drops, water, dust, and harsh environments, often built with IP68/IP69 ratings and reinforced frames. In such phones, durability matters more than slim designs and cameras. These phones are usually preferred by outdoor workers, trekkers, the army, or police officers. Brands like Blackview, Cubot, Oscal, and Ulefone offer dedicated rugged models available in Nepal. Used/Refurbished Smartphones – Pre-owned devices sold at lower prices, often flagship models from previous years. Budget-conscious buyers can access premium features like better cameras and build quality at a fraction of the original cost. This remains a popular option in Nepal, with refurbished iPhones and older Samsung Galaxy models commonly sold through local retailers. Before purchasing, buyers should verify the phone's condition, battery health, and warranty status. Mobile Price in Nepal - Updated 2026 Here is the list of updated mobile prices in Nepal as of now. So, if you are planning to buy a smartphone in 2026, it’s best to purchase only if it’s an immediate need. Otherwise, holding onto your current device for a bit longer could be a smarter decision as the market stabilises. Also Read: Best Phones Under Rs. 20,000 in Nepal (Updated 2026) Best Phones Under Rs. 30,000 in Nepal (Updated 2026) Best Mobile Phones Under Rs. 40,000 in Nepal [Updated 2026] Understanding Smartphone Price Segments in Nepal Budget Smartphones (< NPR 25,000) Budget smartphones in Nepal are usually priced between NPR 10,000 and 25,000 and are ideal for first-time smartphone buyers and casual users. They handle social media, light gaming, and everyday apps efficiently. Brands like Redmi, Samsung, Realme, Vivo, Honor, and Tecno dominate this segment. Keep in mind that the processors and cameras are decent but not great. Midrange Smartphones (NPR 25,000–55,000) Midrange devices offer better displays (OLED), faster processors, and improved cameras. This segment is ideal for users who want value-for-money smartphones with smooth performance. A wide range of options from Xiaomi, Samsung, Realme, Honor, and Vivo is available here, offering the right balance of price and specs. Midrange phones are generally phones under NPR 55000 but above NPR 25000. Premium Midrange Smartphones (NPR 55,000–100,000) These phones offer near-flagship performance at a lower cost. Expect premium designs paired with high-refresh-rate displays (typically 120Hz or higher) that make everyday scrolling and gaming feel noticeably smoother. Under the hood, they're powered by flagship-grade processors capable of handling demanding games and heavy multitasking with ease. Their cameras are also a step up, often featuring larger sensors, better low-light performance, and more refined image processing compared to budget and mid-range options. Ideal for users seeking a premium experience from phones under NPR 100,000. Flagship Smartphones (Above NPR 100,000) Flagship phones such as the Samsung Galaxy S series, Apple iPhones, OnePlus, Xiaomi, Vivo, and Honor deliver ultimate performance, superior cameras, and the best displays available. They come equipped with the latest processors, premium build materials, and extended software support, ensuring a smooth experience for years. This segment is for users who want the latest and greatest technology, regardless of price. It's best suited for professionals, content creators, and tech enthusiasts who prioritise the best possible experience over cost savings. Also Read: Which phone is best under 25000 in Nepal? - (2026) Best Phones Under Rs. 50,000 in Nepal (Updated 2026) How to Choose the Best Smartphone for You? Choosing the right brand for yourself seems complicated for many, but it isn't. The suitable phone is something that fits in your budget and meets the requirements you have. Firstly, noticing your requirements can help narrow down the options and find the phone that offers the best value for your money. You can follow these steps to choose the best phone: Set your budget - Deciding how much you're willing to spend narrows down the choices and makes the buying process far more manageable. Students can typically find everything they need in the NPR 20,000–35,000 range, while working professionals often prefer NPR 35,000–70,000 for better cameras and performance. Those wanting a premium or flagship experience should look above NPR 70,000. Once your budget is fixed within the right category, you can focus only on models that match your needs instead of getting overwhelmed by endless options. Choose the right display size and quality- if you enjoy high-quality streaming and gaming, an AMOLED display is worth prioritising for its sharper colours and better contrast. For basic day-to-day use, a compact display with an LCD panel works just as well and is usually more affordable. Refresh rate also matters here, as a 90Hz or 120Hz screen makes scrolling and gaming feel noticeably smoother. Check the processor and RAM - Today, a phone with a decent processor and 4–6GB of RAM is enough for daily use like calling, browsing, and social media. However, 8GB or more is better suited for gaming, multitasking, and heavier apps that demand more power. Choosing the right balance here ensures your phone stays smooth and doesn't lag even after a year or two of use. Consider camera performance - While selecting a camera, don't just look at higher megapixel counts, as sensor quality often matters more than raw numbers. Checking sample photos and real user reviews gives a much better sense of actual image quality. Features like optical image stabilisation and low-light performance can make a bigger difference than a flashy spec sheet. Look at battery life and charging speed - A 5,000mAh or larger battery paired with fast charging support means less time worrying about your phone dying mid-day. Fast charging is especially useful for those with busy schedules who can't afford to wait hours for a full charge. Battery efficiency also depends on the chipset, so a good processor paired with a large battery gives the best overall experience. Ensure enough storage - In today's time, a phone should ideally have at least 128GB of storage if you take lots of photos, videos, or install several apps. Higher storage options like 256GB are worth considering if you rarely delete files or rely heavily on offline media. Expandable storage via microSD is also a helpful bonus for those who need extra space without paying a premium. Check software updates and security - Choosing a phone that receives regular software and security updates helps keep your device safer from vulnerabilities. It also ensures your phone feels fresh and doesn't become outdated too quickly. Brands that commit to multiple years of updates, like Samsung and Apple, generally offer better long-term value. Consider 5G connectivity and other essential features - Even if 5G isn't fully available everywhere yet, choosing a 5G-ready phone future-proofs your purchase as network coverage continues to expand. Other essentials like NFC, a good in-display fingerprint scanner, and stereo speakers can also significantly improve daily usability. Paying attention to these small details often makes a bigger difference in user experience than headline specs alone. Grey vs Authorised Smartphones in Nepal There are two types of smartphones you can buy in Nepal: official (authorised) units and grey market units. Authorised smartphones are officially imported by brand-authorised distributors. With these, you get a valid warranty and, in some cases (especially on high-end phones), even breakage insurance, where the brand may cover screen replacement for a certain period. However, official phones are usually slightly more expensive due to taxes and proper distribution. On the other hand, grey market smartphones are not officially imported. These devices are generally cheaper, but they do not come with a VAT bill or official warranty. This means that if your phone has any issues, you cannot claim free service from authorised service centres, making it a riskier option. So, it ultimately depends on whether you are willing to take that risk for a lower price. How to Identify an Authorised Phone in Nepal You will receive an official VAT bill at the time of purchase. The box will include the MPIA (Mobile Phone Importers Association) hologram. You will also find the authorised distributor’s seal or label on the packaging. Where to Buy Smartphones at the Best Price in Nepal? There are three main ways to buy smartphones in Nepal: offline retail stores, official showrooms, and online platforms. GBN Store You can buy smartphones from the GBN Store. You can get coupon codes, vouchers, discounts, and freebies, making it one of the best platforms to purchase at a lower price. EMI on Smartphones in GBN Store Since the start of 2025, EMI on smartphones in Nepal has become extremely popular. There are two main reasons behind this growth. First, many brands now offer 0% interest EMI, especially on Android smartphones (while iPhones may have a small interest component). This means you don’t have to pay the full amount upfront, making smartphones more accessible. Second, the process is now much easier. You don’t need a credit card: just citizenship and a guarantor are enough. Because of this hassle-free process, EMI adoption has increased rapidly, with a large portion of mid-range, premium mid-range, and flagship phones now being purchased through EMI. In the GBN store, too, we have a hassle-free EMI service for any mobile phone available in the store. So, if you are looking to get a phone on EMI, do browse through the option. EMI has also changed buying behaviour. Instead of buying a mid-range phone, many users now upgrade to a premium mid-range or even a flagship device. For example, if your budget is NPR 40,000, you can pay around 40% as a down payment and purchase a NPR 1 lakh phone, then pay the remaining amount in monthly instalments (around NPR 5,000 per month for a year). If you have a stable income and can comfortably manage monthly payments, EMI is a smart way to get a better device without paying everything upfront. However, if your income is unstable, it’s better to avoid EMI traps and stick to a phone within your budget. Mobile Price in Nepal: Conclusion Mobile phone prices in Nepal vary by smartphone brand. Some brands may offer better smartphones with better specs at lower prices than others. One should explore models in similar price segments, conduct thorough market research, and then purchase a smartphone. For that, you can always count on our buying guides, articles, and YouTube videos to help you choose the best phone for you.
